title: Webinar: The State Of China Tech
gist: Teaser for a Gavekal Technologies webinar (Arthur Kroeber, Laila Khawaja, AJ Cortese) held as Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet in Washington, framing China's tech capabilities around two near-term questions: how close Chinese AI labs are to US frontier models, and whether the US and China can begin negotiating AI-safety rules. The webinar content itself is behind a sign-up wall; only the framing questions, including how far the two powers can unwind their tech interdependence, are available.

themes.theme: Tech at the Trump-Xi Washington summit

insights.claim: China's fast-growing technology capabilities are positioned by Gavekal as a major topic of the September 2026 meeting between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping in Washington.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch summit readouts for technology and AI language — any concrete tech agenda item would signal a shift from pure trade/tariff bargaining toward tech-rule negotiation.
insights.locator: Webinar: The State Of China Tech (intro)

themes.theme: China AI frontier gap and AI-safety talks

insights.claim: Gavekal frames the key near-term US-China tech question as how close Chinese artificial-intelligence labs are to matching US frontier models, implying the gap is narrow enough to be a live, contested question rather than a settled US lead.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Treat the China-US frontier-model gap as an open variable for AI valuation and export-control risk, not a fixed US moat.
insights.quote: how close Chinese artificial-intelligence labs are to matching the US frontier models
insights.locator: Webinar: The State Of China Tech (intro)

insights.claim: Whether the US and China can start negotiating rules on AI safety is flagged by Gavekal as one of the two big current questions surrounding the Trump-Xi meeting.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: The start of bilateral AI-safety talks would mark a thaw in tech rivalry — a potential de-risking signal for China-exposed AI and semiconductor supply chains.
insights.locator: Webinar: The State Of China Tech (intro)

insights.claim: Behind the AI questions, Gavekal sees two bigger issues: the underlying balance of technological power between the US and China, and how far the two tech powers can actually pull apart the thick webs of interdependence that tie them together — implying full decoupling is harder than political rhetoric suggests.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Be skeptical of trades that price clean US-China tech decoupling; residual interdependence limits how fast supply chains can actually separate.
insights.quote: how far can the world's two big tech powers go in pulling apart the thick webs of interdependence that tie them together?
insights.locator: Webinar: The State Of China Tech (intro)
